s08_diagnostic_decomposition.summary: S08 (only scenario with disjoint successive write windows): worker write discipline (vs_prior_published_store) bitwise-intact and oracle scene invariance (addA vs sceneAB) bitwise-intact outside window2; the diagnostic vs_edited_oracle deviations are 100% inside job1's own write window (utci 2300/2300 unique cells max 6.1e-5 degC; tmrt 3326/3326 max 3.1e-5; shadow 0), bit-for-bit identical to job1's measured inside-window local-vs-full drift vs the addA oracle, and the prior_vs_edited_oracle check differs identically (deviation predates job2). cache_anomaly.finding: repo cache manifest altitude_m=0.0 violates the solver's oracle-altitude rule (median DEM 193.05 m > 0 -> 3.0, utci_process.compute_utci lines 868-872); load_site_forcing raises SolverInputError on the repo cache as-is, so the merged worker refuses every job on it
cache_anomaly.resolution: cache rebuilt under /tmp/p5sci/cache_alt3 with altitude_m=3.0 (same lat 30.312645 / lon -97.728679 / utc -5.0); all 26 cached arrays bitwise identical to the repo cache including the persisted solar series (3 m altitude is below float32 visibility in the sun-position terms), so the differential physics is unaffected and the repo cache needs only a manifest-field rebuild

outside_failure_decomposition.mechanism: The failing vs_edited_oracle sub-check is confined to job1's write window. S08 is the only scenario whose second write window is disjoint from the first, so job1's documented local-vs-full ulp drift (graded by SCI-001 tolerances INSIDE its own window) sits OUTSIDE window2 and is graded by the strict outside-window bitwise criterion against the scene2 oracle.

notes: RECORDED OBSERVATION: local window solve differs from full-tile oracle at <=7.25e-05 abs (ulp-scale float32, p95/p99=0, 0 above envelope) in ~0.05% of compared timestep-cells, across all scenarios incl. single-edit S01 — deterministic, within tolerances.py envelope, root cause un-investigated (candidate: arithmetic-ordering differences between windowed and full-tile paths on 500x500 real site; synthetic tiny-site tests were bitwise). Precision note: at UTCI magnitudes (~300 K range) 6.1e-05 is ~16 ulp float32, i.e. multi-operation accumulation reordering, not a single-rounding difference; binary shadow is bitwise-exact in every scenario.

VERDICT RE-DERIVATION: the original harness graded the outside-window vs-edited-oracle comparison bitwise everywhere, which is stricter than the documented gates; verdicts were re-derived per the spec (rule and citations in each part's verdict_basis; original verdicts preserved under harness_strict_verdict). Under the documented criteria: SCI-002's assertion is outside-window bitwise equality vs the PRIOR PUBLISHED STORE, which holds in all 8 scenarios and every job, including S08's disjoint-window chain; the vs-edited-oracle outside numbers are retained as diagnostics with a containment check (deviations outside every written window would be a hard FAIL; the only deviations, in S08, are 100% inside job1's write window).
Per-scenario blocks carry command, per-job mode/wall/windows/dirty-fraction, tolerance metrics from tests/scientific/metrics.py definitions, outside-window exact checks, and the scenario verdict.

Continuous-variable local-mode output is NOT bitwise equal to the full-tile oracle on this real site (max drift 7.2e-5 degC UTCI / 3.1e-5 K Tmrt; shadow bitwise-exact). The synthetic site achieved bitwise; this site does not, because read windows span the full tile (terrain amplitude puts the 6-degree march reach beyond the site diagonal). All drift is graded against tests/scientific tolerances and passes by ~4 orders of magnitude; ring/band metrics show no seam localization (ring max == interior magnitude).

S01-S05 metric blocks were regenerated from the cached published patches and cached oracles after a harness mask-shape fix (boundary ring / distance bands must be computed at full-site extent before cropping); no physics was re-run and no job or oracle output changed (metrics_regenerated_with_fullsite_masks flag on each part).

Wall times are informational only; performance gates belong to P8. Local jobs on this site derive a site-diagonal-capped halo (large terrain amplitude: amaxvalue 228.34 m minus min DSM 183.97 m -> 6-degree march reach exceeds the tile), so read windows span the full site; exactness is unaffected.

No runtime 'halo-raise' event exists in the P5 worker: the halo is derived analytically per job (derived_halo_px per job block) and the analogous safety events are the amaxvalue/halo-sufficiency SolverInputError fallbacks (S05).
The repo cache altitude anomaly is recorded under environment.cache_anomaly; no repo file other than this evidence JSON was created or modified.
